newsitem.title: UK: Marks & Spencer down after trading statement.
newsitem.headline: Marks & Spencer down after trading statement.

text.p: Shares in Marks & Spencer Plc dropped after the retail group issued a long-awaited Christmas trading statement showing sales up 6.8 percent in the five weeks to January 4.
After being down 3-1/2p shortly before the statment came out, the stock retreated further, to be off 9-1/2p at 483-1/2 by 1203 GMT.
Analysts pointed out that the stock had risen 16p yesterday in anticipation of buoyant trading news.
"The share price moved up yesterday with people expecting a very good statement," said Nick Bubb at MeesPierson.
"It was quite a good statement but it disappointed the expectations of some people and the price has come back to a more realistic level."

Marks said clothing sales were up 7.2 percent in the five weeks to January 4, homeware sales rose 27.7 percent and food was up 4.9 percent. In the 17 weeks to January 25, total sales were up 8.1 percent. "Some people were talking about nine percent growth, which in fact wasn't very likely given that food was likely to drag down the average, which has indeed been the case," said Bubb.
Marks said trading in its North American operations had been below expectations, though it said this was in line with other retailers.
